skills.name: Regular past tense spelling
skills.description: Adding -ed with the doubling and y→i rules.

skills.name: Irregular past tense verbs
skills.description: Common verbs that do not take -ed.

ENG_OVERREGULARISE.label: Adds -ed to irregular verbs
ENG_OVERREGULARISE.explanation: Writes 'goed', 'buyed' or 'catched' instead of went, bought, caught.

ENG_NO_DOUBLING.label: Forgets to double the final consonant
ENG_NO_DOUBLING.explanation: Writes 'stoped' or 'planed' instead of stopped, planned.

ENG_Y_TO_I.label: Keeps the y before adding -ed
ENG_Y_TO_I.explanation: Writes 'cryed' or 'studyed' instead of cried, studied.

regular_past.title: Regular past tense spelling
regular_past.big_idea: Most verbs add -ed for the past tense, but two spelling rules change the word first: double a final consonant after a short vowel, and change a final consonant + y to i.
steps: Short verb ending consonant–vowel–consonant (stop, plan): double the last letter, then add -ed.
Verb ending consonant + y (cry, study): change y to i, then add -ed.
Verb ending vowel + y (play): keep the y (played).
regular_past.sense_check: Without doubling, 'stoped' would rhyme with 'hoped'. The double letter keeps the vowel short.

steps: s-t-O-P: short vowel then one consonant.

irregular_past.title: Irregular past tense verbs
irregular_past.big_idea: Some common verbs have their own past form and never take -ed: go → went, buy → bought, eat → ate.
steps: Before adding -ed, ask: is this one of the irregular verbs?
Many irregular verbs change their vowel (sing → sang, drink → drank).
Some change completely (go → went, buy → bought).
Learn them in groups: think/bought/brought/caught/taught all end in -ought or -aught.
irregular_past.sense_check: Nobody says 'I goed to school' in a book or the news. If it sounds like baby talk, it's probably irregular.

steps: It belongs to the -aught group, like teach → taught.
